contract: A logical operation may be retried for 100 ms after its first send with the same idempotency key. Dedupe entries must cover that whole retry horizon, even when the first acknowledgement is lost. The ledger records business mutations; transport timeouts do not roll them back. No secondary durable dedupe exists.

evidenceRequirements.description: Establish any valid causal witness from the supplied code and context; exact driver numbers/order are not required. One evaluator-only witness: The first send commits and stores a key; its acknowledgement is lost. At time40 the local cache evicts a key with a 30 ms TTL, then the retry applies the mutation again. Retention of120 covers the declared100 ms horizon and returns the prior receipt instead. Reusing the same key is insufficient if storage forgets it too early.

Explain at least one relevant boundary or benign path inferable from the supplied code/context; the following evaluator examples are alternatives, not a mandatory unseen checklist: Immediate retry deduplicates; a different key applies independently; a retry just before100 stays deduplicated; events after120 are outside the contract and cannot establish a failure of the100 ms guarantee.

The idempotency guarantee: is local cache retention required to cover the complete configured retry horizon, or is this cache only best-effort duplicate suppression with repeated effects allowed after eviction?

Under this contract: A logical operation may be retried for 100 ms after its first send with the same idempotency key. Dedupe entries must cover that whole retry horizon, even when the first acknowledgement is lost. The ledger records business mutations; transport timeouts do not roll them back. No secondary durable dedupe exists. the traced behavior is a defect. Alternative: If the cache explicitly offers only best-effort duplicate suppression and repeated effects after eviction are permitted, the second mutation after eviction meets that weaker policy; a complete-horizon idempotency guarantee is then absent.
